title: What Are the PalayCheck Key Checks 1 to 9 for Palay?
metaTitle: Palay Key Check 1 to 9: The PalayCheck List Explained
metaDescription: Every palay key check in PhilRice's PalayCheck System, 1 to 9, in PhilRice's words: what to check, when to check it, and why some lists say eight.
excerpt: PhilRice's PalayCheck System lists nine Key Checks for irrigated lowland rice, from good seed to proper drying and storage. Each palay key check is a target you can see or count in your field at a set crop stage. Older editions had eight, and Key Check 9 on postharvest came with a 2019 revision. anee.io, a farm app built for Filipino farmers, can carry every check as a dated task on your cropping calendar.

blocks.text:
PalayCheck is the rice crop management system of the Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice). Many farmers search for it as the palay check system. It covers the main parts of palay farming, from seed and land to harvest and postharvest.

Instead of a recipe, it gives targets. You manage the crop, compare it with each target, then learn why you hit or missed it. Our Filipino guide to [pagtatanim ng palay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-palay) walks the season itself, so this page sticks to the checks.
Key points

items: PalayCheck's 2022 revised edition has nine Key Checks for irrigated lowland rice, transplanted or direct wet seeded.
Each check has a test, a count or a sign, so you mark it achieved or not.
Checks 1 to 4 come around planting, 5 to 7 run through the season, and 8 and 9 come at harvest and after.
Older material says eight, and PhilRice has announced a reworded edition.

blocks.text: The nine palay key checks, in PhilRice's words

Here is the palay key check 1 to 9 list as the 2022 revised edition prints it. We dropped the hyphens and put one word of Key Check 7 plainly. PhilRice's Filipino edition, Sistemang PalayCheck, gives the same nine in Tagalog.

items: **Key Check 1.** Used high quality seeds of a recommended variety.
**Key Check 3.** Practiced synchronous planting after a rest period.
**Key Check 4.** Sufficient number of healthy seedlings.
**Key Check 5.** Sufficient nutrients from tillering to early panicle initiation (EPI) and flowering.
**Key Check 6.** Avoided stress caused by drought or excessive water that could affect the growth and yield of the crop.
**Key Check 7.** No serious yield loss due to pests.
**Key Check 8.** Harvested the crop at the right time.
**Key Check 9.** Dried, cleaned, and stored grains properly.

blocks.text: What does each key check mean, and when is it checked?
PhilRice gives every check an assessment, the test that says achieved or not, and marks the crop stages for it in its Box 4 chart.

blocks.caption: Palay key check table from the PalayCheck System 2022 edition. TPR is transplanted rice, DWSR is direct wet seeded rice.
rows: Seed has a BPI NSQCS certified tag or comes from a reliable source. The variety suits your area or did well in at least two seasons of trials.
After final leveling, no spot holds more than 5 cm of water and no soil shows above it.
The field rested at least 30 days after harvest, and you planted within 14 days of the regular schedule of your irrigation area.

TPR: 20 to 40 kg seed per hectare, then at least 25 hills per square meter by hand or 21 by machine. DWSR: 40 to 60 kg in rows or 60 to 80 kg broadcast, then at least 150 plants per square meter in rows, or 225 to 300 broadcast.
Sowing, then 10 DAT or 15 to 18 DAS
No deficiency or toxicity signs, and at least 300 panicles per square meter for TPR or 350 for DWSR.
Tillering to flowering, count at dough stage
No drought stress from seedling to dough grain, and no stress from too much water in the vegetative phase.
No serious yield loss from insects, diseases, weeds, rats, snails or birds, judged against PhilRice's damage tables.
Grains 85 to 90 percent golden for hand harvest or 90 to 95 percent for a combine, threshed within 1 day (wet season) or 2 days (dry season).
Dried evenly within 12 to 24 hours, premium purity, cleaned and stored at 12 to 14 percent moisture.

blocks.text: Key checks 1 to 4: before and just after planting

These four cost little to get right and a lot to fix later. PhilRice says high quality seed can add 10 percent or more to yield. A poorly prepared field, on the other hand, can yield 5 percent less. See our guides to [choosing a rice variety](/blog/best-rice-variety-for-my-area) and [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation).

Key Check 3 works only as a group. Most insect pests live about 30 days, so a 30 day rest and planting together leave them nothing to eat.
Key checks 5 to 7: through the growing season

These need your eyes in the field every week. Key Check 5 rests on leaf signs, the leaf color chart and the MOET kit, and our [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice) guide turns them into a plan. Drought stress under Key Check 6 shows as rolled leaves, dry tips and fewer than 10 tillers per hill. Key Check 7 is judged against damage levels, not the first insect you see. So start with [integrated pest management](/pests/integrated-pest-management).
Key checks 8 and 9: harvest and after

Harvest too early and milling recovery can drop as low as 53 percent, PhilRice warns. Too late, and the grain shatters. Key Check 9 then asks you to dry within 12 to 24 hours, as our guide to [drying palay](/blog/palay-drying) explains.
How do you check a key check in the field?
PhilRice's rule is short: use a ruler, count or weigh, and do not guess. Then write the numbers down.

items.title: Pick three spots
items.text: Walk a diagonal across the field and choose three sampling spots, each at least 1 m from the dike.

items.title: Count hills at 10 DAT
items.text: In hand transplanted rice, count the hills in a 1 m by 1 m square at each spot and average them. Machine transplanted rice uses a 1.1 m by 0.9 m square.

items.title: Count plants at 15 to 18 DAS
items.text: In direct wet seeded rice, use a 0.5 m by 0.5 m square, average the counts and multiply by four.

items.title: Count panicles at dough stage
items.text: Use three 1 m by 1 m squares again. The average decides Key Check 5.

items.title: Mark it, then ask why
items.text: Give each check a check mark or a cross. Then talk with your group about why, and change that practice next season.

blocks.title: A check mark is not the goal
blocks.text: PhilRice warns that PalayCheck is not simply putting a check or a cross on each Key Check. Learn why one failed: a stand lost to snails needs a different fix from one sown too thin.
Are there eight or nine PalayCheck key checks?

Both numbers are real. In 2011, PhilRice described PalayCheck as eight key checks from land preparation to harvest. After a 2019 revision, the 2022 edition named the added Key Check 9, on postharvest, as one of its notable changes.

In August 2024, PhilRice said an updated edition with revised Key Check statements would come out by 2025. We could not find it posted online as of October 2026, so this page follows the 2022 edition. If your technician uses newer wording, go with theirs.
How can anee.io carry the key checks as tasks?
PalayCheck asks you to manage by targets and keep records at each stage. In anee.io, you write the checks into your season once, and each lot's own day zero dates them.

items: **Write them into a protocol.** In the [Protocol Builder](/features/protocol-builder), add each check as a task on its day count, like the hill count at 10 DAT.
**Let the calendar date them.** A [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar) dates each task from each lot's own day zero.
**Record the result.** On [today's board](/features/daily-farm-tasks), tick the check done and add a photo of the quadrat or a voice note.
**Tag and count.** Tag tasks Key Check 4 and filter by it, or tap two dates to see the days between them.
**Look back.** Note yield and moisture per lot in your [harvest records](/features/harvest-records), then ask Anee, the smart farm technician, for a season report, which uses credits.

blocks.text: To be clear, anee.io is not a PhilRice product. PhilRice has its own PalayCheck App for Android, launched in 2024, with a season calendar, the recommendations and farm records.

blocks.text: Questions about the PalayCheck key checks

items.q: What is the palay check system?
items.a: It is PalayCheck, the rice integrated crop management system of PhilRice. It sets nine Key Checks from seed to storage, each with a test you can do in your own field, and farmers compare results in groups.

Key Check 5: sufficient nutrients from tillering to early panicle initiation and flowering. You pass it with no deficiency or toxicity signs and at least 300 panicles per square meter in transplanted rice, or 350 in direct seeded rice, at dough stage.
PhilRice teaches it in groups of 15 to 25 farmers who meet before, during and after the season around a demonstration field. Ask your municipal agriculturist or the nearest PhilRice station.
